newsitem.title: UK: Moody's cuts short-term ratings of Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Moody's cuts short-term ratings of Thailand.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday it had downgraded Thailand's short-term sovereign ceiling ratings for bank deposits and other short-term obligations to Prime 2 from Prime 1.
As a result of this action, the short-term deposit ratings of Bangkok Bank Plc, Siam Commercial Bank Plc and Thai Farmers Bank have been downgraded from to Prime 2 from Prime 1, Moody's said.
It said the short-term rating of the Kingdom of Thailand's commercial paper programme was similarly affected.

"The downgrade reflects the country's increased vulnerability to a financial shock through the balance of payments as a result of the very rapid and recent accumulation of short-term external debt," Moody's said in a statement.
It also said that the spill-over effects of any financial instability may also have negative implications for Thailand's long-term foreign currency debt ratings.
Moody's sais the onset of financial liberalisation coupled with a relatively rigid foreign exchange rate system had triggered a massive inflow of short-term funding seeking higher yields in Thailand.

"Both Thai and foreign banks, including the BIBFs established in 1993, appear to have borrowed relatively cheap foreign currency-denominated funds to on-lend at higher spreads to Thai domestic borrowers," it said.
Moody's said that a recent slow-down in economic activity and an "unexpectedly poor performance of the export sector" may reveal weaknesses in the financial sector.
"Further, other short-term capital inflows, such as portfolio investments, have added a further potentially destabilising element," it said.

"Thailand's increased exposure to short-dated capital has heightened the risk of potential liquidity strains over the short-to-medium term in the event that creditor sentiment deteriorates, possibly leading to a sharp reversal or curtailment of such capital inflows," it said.
Moody's said Thailand was clearly facing a more difficult macroeconomic environment.

"While the export slowdown largely reflects a cyclical downturn that has impacted other countries in the region, Thailand must yet contend with structural constraints in order to remain internationally competitive," it said, adding that Thailand's political system could impair the ability of government to implement appropriate economic policies.
"In the short-term, Thailand's very high saving rate and comfortable cushion of official foreign currency reserves should mitigate some of the negative aspects," it said.
But its said that unless authorities pursued the appropriate policies to manage the long-term challenges, the country's sound economic fundamentals "could erode over time".
